title: Using multiple UDP remotes
body:
Hello,
I am trying to use MAVSDK to build 2 programs:
- A "client" program which runs on the companion computer on each drone.
- A GroundStation (GS) which can connect to each client.

I am using 2 UDP connections to connect each client to the GS. However, I can create only one UDP remote at a time otherwise it overwrites the existing system (is_single_system in mavsdk_impl.cpp).

How should I connect my GS to the other clients where each program is using Mavsdk.

comments.body: I think you're right: right now MAVSDK can only add one remote. This would need to be updated in the implementation :+1:. Open for contributions, though :innocent:

All right, I will try to implement it in few days.
Thank you for the confirmation 👍🏼

To summarize the UDP connections system in Mavsdk.
- add_udp_connection("IP:PORT"):
    Create a new UdpConnection instance listening to IP:PORT.
    When the first message coming from a new endpoint (IP_ENDPOINT:PORT_ENDPOINT) is received, a new remote is created to send messages to IP_ENDPOINT:PORT_ENDPOINT.
    
- setup_udp_remote(IP, PORT):
    Create a new UdpConnection instance listening to 0.0.0.0:0 (port 0 = random port).
    Then a remote is created to send messages to IP:PORT

When sending a message, the mavsdk_impl iterates over all connections to send the message.
However, if one of the connections is a UDP connection and has no remote, the loop will break even if other connections could send the message.

see [add-multi-udp-remotes](https://github.com/yhabib29/MAVSDK/tree/add-multi-udp-remotes)

In addition, could it be interesting to add a vector of available system IDs for each connection ?

When sending a message to a specific system ID, this will allow to ignore connections which have never see the corresponding system ID.

The reason is that for radio connections, it might be better to preserve the bandwidth from useless messages.

> However, if one of the connections is a UDP connection and has no remote, the loop will break even if other connections could send the message.

That sounds like a bug, right?

> When sending a message to a specific system ID, this will allow to ignore connections which have never see the corresponding system ID.

Yes, I think that would be a good optimization.

title: ArduPilot support limitations
body:
This is used as a tracking issue for ArduPilot incompatibilities.

Some, but not all MAVSDK plugins have ArduPilot support. This ticket will list **known** compatibilities and incompatibilities. If not listed, the state is unknown - It may work, it may not.

Please comment if you have tested functions and can confirm/deny working.

If you would like an ArduPilot feature included in MAVSDK, please contribute.

### Known API **functional** with ArduPilot :

- Telemetry
  - `set_rate_position_async`
  - `set_rate_gps_info_async`
  - `health_all_ok`
  - `subscribe_position`
  - `subscribe_heading`
  - `subscribe_raw_gps`
  - `armed`
- Mission Raw
  - **NOTE:** First mission item must be home position for ArduPilot
  - `upload_mission_async`
  - `subscribe_mission_progress`
  - `clear_mission_async`
  - `start_mission_async`
- Action
  - `arm`
- MAVLink Passthrough
  - `subscribe_message_async`
  - `send_command_int`
- Param
  - `set_param_float`

### Known **Broken** API

- Mission
  - Needs to account for first mission item being home in Ardupilot
- Probably much more :)

comments.body:
Further broken APIs discovered through running Integration Tests with APM-SITL:
- Action

```c++
- takeoff             // Results in Error:     command unsupported (21). (mavlink_commands.cpp:187)

- land                // Results in Error:  command unsupported (21). (mavlink_commands.cpp:187)

- set_takeoff_altitude // Results in Error:    Error: Retrying failed get param busy timeout: 
                                  // MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT (mavlink_parameters.cpp:793)
				 //		 sending again, retries to do: 3  (MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT). (mavlink_parameters.cpp:780) 

- goto_location  // Results in Error:  command denied (192). (mavlink_commands.cpp:180)
```

There are probably more but need to fix these basic functions before moving to more advanced ones.

These are things that you would need to address on the Ardupilot side. The design goal of MAVSDK is to implement the MAVLink standard (and in the process address things that are not properly standardized, e.g. we're working on a scheme for common flight modes to be able to rip out stack-specific flight modes in MAVSDK).

These examples you are listing can be added to the flight stack, without even having to remove any existing functionality or impact existing users of the flight stack. We're more than happy to help with examples or suggestions how to do this, so this is not a nicer way to say no, but encouraging you by all means to tackle it with our support.

Otherwise what will happen is that MAVSDK has to cater to too many ways of doing things, too intense testing and will burn out its maintainers. The fact that this happened with QGC shows us that it is not a hypothetical problem and is why we're so adamant about it from a TSC perspective. It is all about protecting the integrity and long-term maintainability of the project.

title: REQUEST_MESSAGE vs custom getters like REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION
body:
It's currently part of the [list for MAVSDK v2](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2002), and though I don't think I can contribute an implementation, I think I can contribute a (relatively informed) opinion.

TL;DR: I don't think this can go in MAVSDK v2 :see_no_evil:.

#### We cannot detect what the receiver supports

There is no way to detect if the receiver supports `REQUEST_MESSAGE`, because the requested message could have been requested by someone else, or it could be transmitted spontaneously by the receiver. So making statistics to try to guess stuff like "was this `CAMERA_INFORMATION` message an answer to my request, or is it a coincidence?" is probably not worth it by far.

Also each message is independent. So even if we managed to detect that `REQUEST_MESSAGE` is supported for `CAMERA_INFORMATION`, it would not say anything about e.g. `REQUEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

#### What we can do

* Push the receivers to support both messages (i.e. the drone should support both `REQUEST_MESSAGE(<camera_information>)` and `REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION`.
* Keep the old way in MAVSDK until we feel like we can completely drop it.

In other words, the implementation work is not on the MAVSDK side, but on the receiver side (e.g. make sure that PX4/Ardupilot support the newer messages, make sure that cameras do, push proprietary players to do it).

Some day, maybe we will feel comfortable in dropping the old way and telling people "well if your drone does not support the new way, that's your problem".

title: Set rate position and attitude_euler not working with ArduPilot

comments.body:
Hello @julianoes ,
Is this issue open for contribution? I am a first-time contributor and would be happy to work on it if you could assign it to me.
@lakhmanisahil sure go ahead and make a pull request if you have a solution for it. I'm not working on it at the moment.
Thanks, @julianoes . I am looking into this issue and will aim to submit a PR.

Hi @julianoes, I've been studying the source (no hardware yet) and I think the fix should go inside `telemetry_impl.cpp`. All the `set_rate_xxx` functions call `_system_impl->set_msg_rate()` / `set_msg_rate_async()`, which internally send `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` (cmd 511) — ArduPilot doesn't ACK this reliably on serial links. 

I can see `_system_impl->effective_autopilot()` is already used in `process_sys_status()`, so the fix would be to check `effective_autopilot() == Autopilot::ArduPilot` and fall back to `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM` instead for the affected rate setters. 

Planning to open a PR regarding this. Does that approach look right to you?

Files I'd change: [`telemetry_impl.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp) · [`telemetry_impl.h`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.h)

Investigated the ArduPilot source — `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` is fully supported for both `ATTITUDE` and `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT`. The command is correctly handled, ACKed, and applied.

The actual root cause is **GCS stream rate override**: when another GCS application (MAVProxy, QGC, Mission Planner) on the same MAVLink link sends `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM`, ArduPilot's `initialise_message_intervals_for_stream()` overwrites all individual message intervals in that stream group. So the rate set by MAVSDK gets silently clobbered.

Confirmed by ArduPilot issues: ArduPilot/ardupilot#17046, ArduPilot/ardupilot#19761, ArduPilot/ardupilot#28550.

**Workarounds:**
- Set `MAVn_OPTIONS` bit 2 (NOSTREAMOVERRIDE) on the ArduPilot port used by MAVSDK
- Ensure no other GCS sends `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM` on the same link
- When using SITL with MAVProxy, start with `--streamrate=-1`

This is not a MAVSDK bug — it's a user configuration issue on the ArduPilot side.
Oh, this makes more sense. Thanks for investigating @PavelGuzenfeld. I'll close this issue then.
